title: Your fingerprints aren't in your genes
hook: Right now, your fingertips are pressing against your past.
script: Right now, your fingertips are pressing against your past. Identical twins share the same DNA, yet their different fingerprints? The ridges on your fingertips are shaped by tiny random forces as you press against the womb, not in your genes. The Vasilev quadruplets’ identical DNA couldn’t write the same prints. The pressure on your skin varies by as little as 1-2 mmHg to create unique ridges. Your phone is unlocking a pattern that isn’t even written in your genes. The one mark police use to tell people apart is decided by randomness, not heredity. So if someone asks, whose fingerprint is this?
